maya.support: OK — copy/paste these minimal steps to the customer. Keep it tiny so they actually run it. Ask them to attach the outputs to the ticket (INC-4123).

maya.support: 1) Run this curl (captures headers + body) so we can see request id and status.

```bash
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hello"}' \
  --max-time 60 -v --trace-ascii curl-debug.txt \
```

maya.support: 2) If they use our HTTP SDKs, ask them to enable verbose debug. Examples below. Also ask for client app logs and the exact local timestamp when the failing requests happened.

maya.support: Python (requests) minimal:

```python
# save as repro.py
import os
import requests

headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
data = {"model": "redwood-1", "input": "hello from repro"}
resp = requests.post("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", json=data, headers=headers, timeout=30)
print(resp.status_code, resp.headers.get("X-Request-Id"))
print(resp.text)
```

maya.support: Node (fetch) minimal:

```js
// node repro.js (requires node 18+ or node-fetch)
const url = 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate';
const body = { model: 'redwood-1', input: 'hello from node' };
const res = await fetch(url, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify(body),
  timeout: 30000
});
console.log(res.status, res.headers.get('x-request-id'));
console.log(await res.text());
```

maya.support: Go minimal:

```go
// go run repro.go
package main
import (
  "bytes"
  "fmt"
  "io/ioutil"
  "net/http"
  "os"
)
func main() {
  apiKey := os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY")
  body := []byte(`{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hello from go"}`)
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", bytes.NewReader(body))
  req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+apiKey)
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
  client := &http.Client{}
  resp, err := client.Do(req)
  if err != nil { fmt.Println("ERROR:", err); return }
  defer resp.Body.Close()
  b, _ := ioutil.ReadAll(resp.Body)
  fmt.Println(resp.StatusCode, resp.Header.Get("X-Request-Id"))
  fmt.Println(string(b))
}
```

maya.support: 3) Debug env/flags we ask them to enable: set REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=1 or export REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=true (for our official SDKs) and re-run. Also attach the curl-debug.txt from the curl command above.

ingrid.sre: Add `-v` or `--trace-ascii` for curl TLS handshake info if they can share it. If using Go, `GODEBUG=http2debug=1` can help but warn customer about verbose output.

sam.engineering: Quick checklist for support: request id, curl-debug.txt, SDK debug log, client app logs (timestamps), exact API path + payload, and whether they are behind a proxy or corporate firewall. If they can reproduce, include the full curl output (headers + body).

maya.support: I'll post those snippets to the customer and ask them to reply in INC-4123 with attachments. If they get a 502 again, ask for the X-Request-Id and the timestamp in ISO format.

alex.h: Perfect — thanks. I'll follow up once customer uploads. :thumbsup:
